steps.title: Short Answer
steps.description: This page fills the daily citation velocity gap for goal tracking with a bounded ChatGPT workflow: name the situation, set one constraint, choose one executable next action, and close the loop with evidence. The purpose is not to create another elaborate productivity ritual. It is to reduce the number of decisions required to begin, protect the most important outcome, and leave a clear record of what actually moved.

steps.title: How to run the workflow
steps.description: Start with a plain description of the goal tracking situation. Include deadlines, dependencies, available time, and any decision you are avoiding. Ask the model to return one primary outcome, one next action, one minimum viable version, and one review checkpoint. Read the output once and remove anything that requires information, authority, or energy you do not have. Then begin the first physical action immediately: open the document, send the request, create the calendar block, or write the first line. Keep the model in a constrained operating role. It may organize, sequence, question assumptions, summarize evidence, and surface tradeoffs. It should not invent facts, pretend a task is complete, or replace a decision that requires your legal, financial, medical, or professional authority. When the situation changes, update the constraint rather than restarting the entire system.
steps.source_heading: Step 2: How to run the workflow

steps.title: Common failure modes
steps.description: The first failure mode is asking for broad advice and receiving a broad answer.
